title: Private VPC control-plane buyer objections & positioning brief
content:
Purpose:
This is a working GTM brief focused on positioning Redwood Private (VPC / on-prem) to regulated buyers. Goal: give AE/SEs an objection playbook, one-line/three-line value props, competitive differentiation, and a short list of follow-up asks for product.

Audience & personas:
- Platform Security / Infrastructure (primary): cares about network controls, auditability, key custody, isolation, and support model.
- Compliance / Risk: wants certs, evidence, data residency and minimal third-party egress.
- ML Engineering / SRE: cares about model parity, latency, integration complexity, and ops burden.
- Procurement: TCO, contract length, SLAs, termination/exit.

Top-level positioning (one-line / three-line):
- One-line: Redwood Private gives you an enterprise-grade inference control plane you can host in your VPC or on-prem, with customer-managed keys, audit-grade logs, and predictable SLAs.
- Three-line: Ship LLM features while keeping all control over your network and keys. Redwood provides a customer-controlled control plane (optional control plane components you run inside your VPC), verified model variants for parity with hosted API, and enterprise operational tooling (tracing, rollout policies, cost breakdowns) that integrates with your SIEM and KMS.

Typical buyer objections and rebuttals (short playbook):
1) "We can't have a vendor control plane talking to our cluster; it violates policy."
   - Rebuttal: Offer the offline/private control plane option: we provide a self-hosted control plane bundle that runs entirely in your environment. If you need a managed control plane, we can sign an architecture-level NDA and outline exact traffic flows.
   - Ask for info: Which data flows are disallowed? (metadata only vs. tokens).

2) "How do we guarantee no data egress or leakage to vendor services?"
   - Rebuttal: Redwood Private supports an air-gapped deployment and VPC-only endpoints. Our audit artifacts include per-request hashes and KMS-wrapped keys. Provide example architecture diagram; propose a PoC in our lab or a short onsite proof.
   - Ask for info: Is there any allowed telemetry? If yes, what telemetry is acceptable (error metrics only, anonymized latency)?

3) "Key management: we need HSM/KMS-backed keys under our control."
   - Rebuttal: We integrate with customer KMS/HSM (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault, and on-prem HSM via PKCS11). Customer keys can be used to encrypt model assets and request logs.
   - Ask for info: Which KMS/HSM type and rotation policy do you require?

4) "Operational burden — we don’t want to run another complex stack."
   - Rebuttal: Redwood Private comes with opinionated deployment manifests (Helm/Terraform), automated upgrade tooling, and a runbook. For enterprise customers we offer an onboarding engagement (SRE handoff + runbook).
   - Ask for info: What's your team's maintenance window cadence and preferred upgrade policy?

5) "Model parity vs hosted API — will outputs match?"
   - Rebuttal: We provide model version pins and quantization profiles used in Hosted. We'll run a shared evaluation prompt set and provide regression alerts. If strict parity required, we can support a model-sync process and CI checks.

Competitive notes (quick matrix):
- Large cloud vendors: 
  - Strengths: familiar contracts, native KMS/identity; weakness: often charged separately for infra, vendor lock-in on model features.
  - Our angle: unified inference interface across Hosted/Dedicated/Private — customers get the same API/rollouts regardless of environment.
- Inference runtime vendors (self-hosted runtimes + ops):
  - Strengths: strong on performance; weakness: lack product-level features like rollouts, token-level cost insights, and evals.
  - Our angle: combine runtime performance with product features (rollouts, tracing, cost allocation).
- Boutique compliance-focused vendors: 
  - Strengths: tight compliance controls, but often missing scale/cost tooling.
  - Our angle: we match compliance controls while giving predictable unit economics and tooling for production ML.

Proof points / assets to surface in sales cycles:
- Deployment templates (Helm + example VPC configs).
- Redacted audit log sample showing per-request metadata + non-sensitive hashes.
- One-pager: "Control plane options — managed vs self-hosted" (link to Confluence-1234).
- Benchmark: latency parity for an Llama-2 13B variant on common infra (internal benchmark ID: bench-2025-09-vpc).
- Customer references: (placeholder) finance customer who ran air-gapped PoC — request to legal to un-redact.

Technical details / talking points for SEs:
- Control plane: can be deployed as a set of k8s controllers in customer cluster, or run on an isolated management subnet with private peering. Control-plane -> serving-host traffic can be strictly outbound-only and authenticated via mTLS.
- Telemetry: default is no request payload telemetry sent to Redwood. Optional telemetry toggles: error-only, metrics-only, full (customer consent).
- Key lifecycle: keys used for model disk encryption, KV cache encryption, and optional request envelope encryption. Keys are never exported to Redwood-managed HSM when customer-managed keys are enabled.
- Auditing: support for syslog/Splunk/Elastic ingest; logs contain request ids, model id, token counts, latencies, and normalized request hashes (no PII).

Pricing & procurement notes:
- Pricing model should include: one-time onboarding fee for Private installation + subscription per reserved capacity band + optional premium support.
- Negotiation levers: onboarding scope, retention of telemetry, commit terms, runbook SLAs.

Objections we need product work on (open items / TODOs):
- Clear, short architecture diagrams for both fully air-gapped and VPC-managed control plane variants. (Owner: Diego Morales, JIRA-PRIV-88)
- Configurable telemetry templates (customer toggle presets) — UX flows in console and docs. (Owner: Lena Kaur)
- Ship a redactable audit log sample and a standardized SOC2/ISO evidence bundle for sales. (Owner: Ethan Brooks)

Sales collateral & quick scripts:
- Email subject lines: "Redwood Private: Run inference inside your VPC (no data egress)" / "Proof: air-gapped inference in 5 days — sample runbook"
- Elevator pitch for execs: "Want LLM features without vendor data exposure? Redwood Private gives you the same developer API and rollout tools while keeping keys, network, and audit trails inside your control."
- Demo flow: 1) Show Console: toggle telemetry and audit; 2) Show config: KMS selection and model pinning; 3) Run a parity demo against hosted outputs; 4) Show logs being forwarded to customer SIEM.

Notes to self / meeting prep checklist:
- Bring architecture diagram + sample helm values.
- Confirm which data types customer considers sensitive (tokens vs. metadata).
- Prepare legal FAQ on data residency & contractual language.
- Ask: Do you require a written attestation that Redwood never stores request payloads when customer-managed keys + air-gap enabled?

Unresolved questions (requires product / legal):
- Formal attestation language we can promise regarding non-storage of request payloads.
- Minimum customer infra footprint (GPU/specs) for our recommended model variants.

Bottom line (single sentence for pitch decks):
- Redwood Private: enterprise inference with your controls — same API, same rollouts, your network and keys.
